or_callahans_the.blurb: A ridge of sandstone cliffs and pinnacles west of Roseburg in southwest Oregon, spread over a few miles. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a good helping of trad and a few boulders and top-ropes. Grades run from 5.6 up to the low 5.12s, and the thickest concentration sits around 5.10, with plenty of 5.7 to 5.9 as well. Sitting high on the ridge, even short routes feel exposed, with wide views toward the Cascades. Winter climbing is popular, since sunny days are often found above the valley fog. Troll's Throne is a slabby sandstone wall ringed by Douglas fir, so it dries slowly after rain. Britt Nichols County Park holds the most routes, with Mind Planet, Fantasy Island and Turtle Rock close behind.

wa_seattle_and_seattle_eastside.blurb: An urban grouping of small climbing spots around Seattle, stretching from Auburn in the south to Edmonds in the north and east to Issaquah and Duvall. Many of the climbs are on built features such as campus walls, park structures and a skate park rather than natural cliffs. Bouldering is the largest share, mostly V0 to V3 with a few harder problems, followed by sport, trad and top-rope. Roped grades are mostly 5.8 to 5.10. Marymoor Park in Redmond has a small outdoor wall with sport routes and boulders, used as a place to train for real rock. The University of Washington campus, Marymoor, Seattle itself and the Kent skate park are the largest pockets.

_expect.name: Mt. Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans) Bouldering

co_mt_evans_bouldering.blurb: High alpine granite bouldering on Mt. Blue Sky, roughly thirty miles west of Denver, with every block above 10,000 feet. Bouldering is all there is, and the grades span a very wide range: a thin supply of V0 to V3, a thick middle from V4 to V9, and a serious tail of V10 and harder for top boulderers. The granite is highly featured, with rough texture, incut edges and a few knobs. The season is short, running roughly June to September depending on snow, and the weather brings fast storms, wind, intense sun and thin air. Approaches are hard work over talus and rough ground. Area A and Lincoln Lake hold most of the problems, with Echo Boulders a distant third.

co_west_ridge_the.blurb: A long diagonal cliff band on the south side of South Boulder Creek in Eldorado Canyon State Park, built of southwest-facing sandstone that is far wider than it is tall. Nearly all of it is trad, with a few sport lines and boulders, and the grades run from 5.6 up through 5.12, concentrated between 5.8 and 5.11. Climbs range from short highballs to a handful of multi-pitch lines, with the faces, dihedrals, slabs, overhangs and cracks all represented. Spread-out routes and a tight spread of difficulties make it a good place for moderate trad climbers. Temperature shifts with aspect, shade and altitude. The ridge is divided into lettered sections from the base to the top, and the middle sections are the biggest.

ca_bishop_peak.blurb: A volcanic plug in San Luis Obispo, the tallest of the Nine Sisters, a chain of peaks that runs toward Morro Bay. The rock is dacite, evenly featured with a bit of crack, mostly face, and plenty of slab. The climbing is varied: sport and trad are about equal, a good block of boulder problems sits alongside, and there are a few top-ropes. Roped grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, with the greatest number at 5.10, and boulders are mostly V0 to V6. It is the most popular local cragging spot in the county and lies close to town. P-Wall, Cracked Wall and Shadow Rock are the largest crags, and Bishop Peak Bouldering holds the most problems.

ca_rattlesnake_canyon.blurb: A desert canyon in the northern part of Joshua Tree National Park, at the southeast corner of Indian Cove, with crags on the canyon walls and on the hillside above. Trad is the main event, with a solid number of sport routes, some top-ropes, and a scattering of boulders. Roped grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, with the largest group around 5.10. Corral Wall and Valley of Kings are trad-heavy, while Iceberg Boulder Area holds boulders and some sport. Approaches vary a lot, from a few minutes to well over an hour. It is a bit quieter than some of the better-known Indian Cove formations, and Indian Cove as a whole sits lower and sheltered, so it suits cool days.
